info.desc: Hybrid Theory is the debut album by the American rock band Linkin Park, released on October 24th, 2000 through Warner Bros. Records. The album was a huge commercial success, selling over 10 million units in the United States alone and peaking at number two on the Billboard 200 while also reaching high positions on other charts worldwide, despite receiving mixed reviews from publications. It has also sold 24 million copies worldwide as of 2009, including over 10 million in the U.S. which makes it the band's best-selling album, the second best-selling album of the 21st century so far, and the .

podcast.body: Released in 2000, this album marked the band's debut and achieved significant commercial success, selling 30 million copies worldwide. It established the band's initial presence in the music industry. "Hybrid Theory, the first album, sold 30 million."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on October 20, 2000, this album was a monumental success, selling five million copies in its first year and over 30 million worldwide. It topped charts in New Zealand (number one), and reached number two in the US, Germany, and Australia, also charting in the top ten in Canada, Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, Norway, Scotland, Sweden, and Switzerland. The album earned three Grammy nominations, winning one for "Crawling" in the Best Hard Rock Performance category. Its success was attributed to the band's strong music, Mike Shinoda's rapping, and their firm stance against various "stupid suggestions" from label representatives regarding their image and sound, such as removing rap elements or altering their logo. "That record was released on October 20th of 2000."

podcast.body: Released on October 24, 2000, this debut album sold over 18 million copies in the US and 1.3 million in Canada, with global sales estimated between 35 and 38 million records, making it the best-selling debut rock record of the new century. It was completed in just four weeks and, despite being critically dismissed as "more of the same old new metal," it was embraced by fans for its blend of rapping, scratching, screaming, big riffs, beats, and a catchy pop sensibility. "Since their first album was released on October 24, 2000, Lincoln Park is sold over 18 million albums in the US and another 1.3 million in Canada."

podcast.body: This album sold over 4.8 million copies in 2001, at a time when more than 26 million people were actively using Napster for file-sharing. The album's strong sales occurred despite the significant impact of peer-to-peer sharing on the music industry. "As Lincoln Park was on their way to selling more than 4.8 million copies of their hybrid theory album in 2001, more than 26 million people were using Napster."
